units.title: Place Value and Big Numbers
units.blurb: Read, compare and round numbers to a million, and add and subtract them with the standard algorithm.

units.title: Multi-Digit Multiplication
units.blurb: Compare with "times as many" and multiply larger numbers with area models and partial products.

units.title: Division with Remainders
units.blurb: Divide up to four-digit numbers by one-digit numbers and decide what a remainder means.

units.title: Factors, Multiples and Patterns
units.blurb: Find factor pairs and multiples, sort primes from composites, and follow rules.

units.title: Equivalent Fractions
units.blurb: Make equivalent fractions and compare fractions with different denominators.

units.title: Adding Fractions and Mixed Numbers
units.blurb: Add and subtract fractions with like denominators and multiply a fraction by a whole number.

units.title: Decimals
units.blurb: Write tenths and hundredths as decimals and compare them.

units.title: Measurement and Conversions
units.blurb: Convert units, solve measurement problems, and use area and perimeter formulas.

units.title: Lines, Angles and Shapes
units.blurb: Draw and name lines and angles, measure angles, and sort shapes.

topics.title: Each Place Is Ten Times the Next
topics.short: A digit is worth ten times what it would be one place to the right.
topics.trouble: Children think the 7 in 700 is worth 7 tens more than in 70, instead of ten times as much.

topics.title: Reading and Writing Large Numbers
topics.short: Read and write numbers to a million in digits, words and expanded form.
topics.trouble: Children drop or add zeros when a period is empty, writing "forty thousand six" as 4,006 or 400,006.

topics.title: Comparing Large Numbers
topics.short: Compare from the greatest place down.

topics.title: Rounding to Any Place
topics.short: Round to the nearest ten, hundred, thousand and beyond.
topics.trouble: Children round every digit to the right separately, or change digits to the left of the rounding place.

topics.title: The Standard Algorithm for Adding and Subtracting
topics.short: Add and subtract multi-digit numbers column by column.
topics.trouble: Children regroup across several zeros incorrectly, as in 6,000 − 2,347.

topics.title: Times as Many
topics.short: 15 is 3 times as many as 5.
topics.trouble: Children treat "3 times as many" as "3 more than."

topics.title: Comparison Word Problems
topics.short: Decide whether a comparison is "more than" or "times as many," then solve.

topics.title: Multiplying by 10, 100 and 1,000
topics.short: Each factor of 10 moves every digit one place to the left.

topics.title: Multiplying with an Area Model
topics.short: Split a factor by place value and add the partial products.

topics.title: Multiplying by a One-Digit Number
topics.short: Multiply numbers up to four digits by one digit.
topics.trouble: Children forget to add the regrouped amount after multiplying the next digit.

topics.title: Multiplying Two Two-Digit Numbers
topics.short: Find four partial products and add them.
topics.trouble: Children multiply only tens by tens and ones by ones, so 23 × 14 becomes 212.

topics.title: Division with Remainders
topics.short: Some totals do not split evenly; the leftover is the remainder.
topics.trouble: Children leave a remainder larger than the divisor.

topics.title: Dividing Tens and Hundreds
topics.short: 240 ÷ 6 is 24 tens ÷ 6, which is 4 tens.

topics.title: Dividing with Partial Quotients
topics.short: Take away easy multiples of the divisor until little is left.

topics.title: Long Division by a One-Digit Number
topics.short: Divide, multiply, subtract and bring down, place by place.
topics.trouble: Children skip a 0 in the quotient, so 618 ÷ 6 comes out as 13 instead of 103.

topics.title: What to Do with a Remainder
topics.short: Drop it, round up or report it, depending on the question.
topics.trouble: Children answer "8 R2 buses" or round down when the extra people still need a seat.

topics.title: Multistep Word Problems
topics.short: Solve problems with several operations and check with an estimate.

topics.title: Factor Pairs
topics.short: List all pairs of whole numbers that multiply to a number.
topics.trouble: Children stop before finding every pair, or forget 1 and the number itself.

topics.title: Multiples
topics.short: A multiple of 6 is 6 times a whole number.
topics.trouble: Children mix up factors and multiples, listing 2 and 3 as multiples of 12.

topics.title: Prime and Composite Numbers
topics.short: A prime has exactly two factors: 1 and itself.
topics.trouble: Children think 1 is prime, or that every odd number is prime.

topics.title: Patterns from a Rule
topics.short: Make a pattern from a rule and notice features the rule does not say.

topics.title: Equivalent Fractions by Multiplying
topics.short: Multiply top and bottom by the same number: the pieces get smaller, the amount stays.
topics.trouble: Children add the same number to the top and bottom, thinking 2/3 equals 4/5.

topics.title: Simplest Form
topics.short: Divide top and bottom by a common factor to use fewer, larger pieces.
topics.trouble: Children divide the numerator and denominator by different numbers.

topics.title: Comparing with 1/2 and 1
topics.short: Use 1/2 and 1 as landmarks to compare fractions.

topics.title: Comparing Any Two Fractions
topics.short: Rename with a common denominator or numerator, then compare.
topics.trouble: Children compare only the numerators or only the denominators of unlike fractions.

topics.title: Breaking Fractions into Sums
topics.short: 5/8 = 1/8 + 1/8 + 3/8 and other ways.

topics.title: Adding and Subtracting Like Fractions
topics.short: Add or subtract the numerators; the size of the pieces stays the same.
topics.trouble: Children add the denominators too, so 1/5 + 2/5 becomes 3/10.

topics.title: Mixed Numbers and Fractions Greater Than 1
topics.short: 2 1/3 and 7/3 name the same amount.
topics.trouble: Children convert 2 1/3 to 3/3 by multiplying only the whole number or adding 2 + 1.

topics.title: Adding and Subtracting Mixed Numbers
topics.short: Add wholes and fractions, regrouping a whole when needed.
topics.trouble: When regrouping in 3 1/5 − 1 3/5, children turn the borrowed 1 into 10/5 instead of 5/5.

topics.title: Fraction Word Problems
topics.short: Solve stories that add or subtract like fractions.

topics.title: Multiplying a Fraction by a Whole Number
topics.short: 3 × 2/5 is 6 fifths.
topics.trouble: Children multiply both the numerator and the denominator by the whole number, so 3 × 2/5 becomes 6/15.

topics.title: Tenths and Hundredths
topics.short: 3/10 is the same as 30/100.

topics.title: Writing Decimals
topics.short: 0.3 means 3 tenths; 0.03 means 3 hundredths.
topics.trouble: Children write 3 hundredths as 0.3, or 5 tenths as 0.05.

topics.title: Comparing Decimals
topics.short: Compare tenths first, then hundredths.
topics.trouble: Children think a decimal with more digits is larger, so 0.25 seems bigger than 0.3.

topics.title: Converting Larger Units to Smaller
topics.short: 3 feet is 36 inches; 2 kilograms is 2,000 grams.
topics.trouble: Children divide when converting to a smaller unit, because the unit is getting smaller.

topics.title: Measurement Word Problems
topics.short: Solve problems with distance, time, volume, mass and money.

topics.title: Area and Perimeter Formulas
topics.short: Use A = l × w and P = 2l + 2w, and work backward to a missing side.
topics.trouble: Children add the length and width once for perimeter, forgetting the other two sides.

topics.title: Line Plots with Fractions
topics.short: Make line plots in eighths and add or subtract with them.

topics.title: Points, Lines, Segments and Rays
topics.short: Name and draw these basic figures.

topics.title: What an Angle Measures
topics.short: An angle measures the amount of turn; a degree is 1/360 of a full turn.
topics.trouble: Children think longer rays make a bigger angle.

topics.title: Acute, Right and Obtuse Angles
topics.short: Compare angles with a right angle.

topics.title: Measuring Angles with a Protractor
topics.short: Line up the center and a zero ray, then read the scale.
topics.trouble: Children read the wrong scale on the protractor, so an acute angle is reported as 130°.

topics.title: Adding Angles
topics.short: Angles that fit together add; find a missing part.

topics.title: Parallel and Perpendicular Lines
topics.short: Parallel lines never meet; perpendicular lines meet at right angles.

topics.title: Sorting Shapes by Sides and Angles
topics.short: Classify triangles and quadrilaterals by parallel sides and angle types.

topics.title: Lines of Symmetry
topics.short: A line of symmetry folds a shape onto itself.
topics.trouble: Children draw a diagonal of a rectangle as a line of symmetry.
